messages.content: Our cloud bill is up 40% this month. Where do I start?

Start with Cost Explorer grouped by service, then by usage type. The usual suspects: NAT gateway data processing, S3 request and transfer charges, idle or oversized RDS instances, forgotten EBS snapshots, and CloudWatch log ingestion. Tell me which line grew the most.
NAT gateway data processing grew by about $1,900.

Then check what traffic goes through the NAT. A frequent cause is private subnets reaching S3 through the NAT instead of directly. Add an S3 gateway endpoint to the VPC; gateway endpoints have no hourly or data charge.

I added the gateway endpoint yesterday, but NAT bytes had not dropped. Today I found the cause: the endpoint was not associated with the private route tables. I associated it an hour ago and CloudWatch shows NAT bytes down about 90%. The bill lags by a day, so I cannot see the cost effect yet. Update me, based only on that.

required_facts: Root cause found: the S3 gateway endpoint existed but was not associated with the private route tables, so adding the endpoint alone was not enough
After associating it an hour ago, NAT bytes are down about 90% in CloudWatch (as the user reported)
The saving on the bill is not confirmed yet because billing lags by a day
The other possible causes (S3 requests, RDS, snapshots, log ingestion) have not been checked
critical_omissions: Saying the cost problem is solved or that the savings are confirmed
Saying the other candidate causes were ruled out
Saying the endpoint alone was sufficient
unnecessary_repetition: The list of usual suspects for a cost increase
How gateway endpoints work and that they have no hourly or data charge
